markdown:
## Summary
I'll add a saved-search picker plus a "Save Search" icon and a "Manage" icon to the top of the collection container, backed only by **session storage** (no REST), and two new dialogs — one to name/save the current filter, one to list/delete saved searches. Saving snapshots the current `filterCriterion`; applying one writes it back so the list re-filters.

## How it works today
The page uses `oj-sp-smart-search` (slot `search`) bound to `$variables.filterCriterion`; the equipment list DPV reads that variable through its constructor binding, so any change re-filters the server-side list. The search band is drawn by the `oj-sp-smart-search-page` template. There is no saved-search concept today.

## What changes
- A saved-search picker, a "Save Search" button and a "Manage" button are added **inside the collection container** (the only place in the template where free markup renders — the template's header band is not ours to add markup to), above the view-toggle bar.
- Two new `oj-dialog`s: **Save Search** (name field + Save) and **Saved Searches** (list with Delete).
- Saved searches live in `$variables.savedSearches`, seeded from `sessionStorage` on page enter, so they survive in-app navigation within the session but are not persisted to any REST service (per your instruction).
- Each saved search stores an `id`, `name` and a snapshot of the current `filterCriterion`. Applying one sets `filterCriterion`.

## The change
- `equipment-master-page.json` — add variables (`savedSearches`, `savedSearchesADP`, `newSearchName`, `selectedSavedSearch`); add a `vbEnter` chain `LoadSavedSearchesChain`; add eventListeners (`onSaveSearch`, `onApplySavedSearch`, `onDeleteSavedSearch`). (`oj-select-single`, `oj-dialog`, `oj-button`, `oj-c-button`, `oj-c-input-text`, `oj-bind-for-each`, `oj-bind-if` already imported.)
- `equipment-master-page.html` — add a saved-search bar at the top of the collection container, and the two dialogs at the end of the file.
- New chains: `LoadSavedSearchesChain.js`, `SaveSearchChain.js`, `ApplySavedSearchChain.js`, `DeleteSavedSearchChain.js`.

## After the change
1. The user applies filters in the smart search (chips) as today.
2. They click the **Save Search** (bookmark) icon → a dialog asks for a name → Save. It appears in the picker.
3. They pick a saved search from the dropdown → the list re-filters to that saved filter.
4. A **Manage** icon opens a dialog listing saved searches with Delete.
5. Saved searches persist across in-app navigation for the session only, lost on browser close — no REST yet.

## Risks
Session-only: saved searches are per-browser-session and not durable or shared. No other page uses these new variables/chains. `filterCriterion` is already the live filter, so applying one is the same mechanism the chips use. None known beyond the temporary-storage caveat.

## How to test
1. Open Equipment Master. Apply one or more facet chips (e.g. Class = Tools).
2. Click the Save Search icon, enter "My Tools", click Save.
3. Clear the chips. Pick "My Tools" from the saved-search dropdown → list re-filters to Tools.
4. Open Manage, click Delete on "My Tools" → it disappears from the dropdown.
5. Navigate away and back within the session → remaining saved searches are still listed.

## Questions
None.
